generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

Consider the function \(f(x)=\tan(2x)\).

The standard tangent function \(y=\tan x\) has period \(\pi\). The factor \(2\) multiplying \(x\) changes the period and the locations of the zeros and vertical asymptotes.

Step 1: Period

For a function of the form \(f(x)=\tan(bx)\), the period is \(\displaystyle \frac{\pi}{|b|}\).

Here, \(b=2\), so the period is \(\displaystyle T=\frac{\pi}{2}\).

Your answer: \(\displaystyle {@ans_period@}\).

The correct answer is \(\displaystyle \frac{\pi}{2}\).

Step 2: Zeros

The tangent function is zero when its argument is an integer multiple of \(\pi\). Therefore,

\(2x=n\pi\), where \(n\in\mathbb{Z}\).

Solving for \(x\) gives \(\displaystyle x=\frac{n\pi}{2}\).

In the interval \(\displaystyle -\frac{\pi}{2}\leq x\leq\frac{\pi}{2}\), the zeros are

\(\displaystyle x=-\frac{\pi}{2},\quad x=0,\quad x=\frac{\pi}{2}\).

Your first zero: \(\displaystyle {@ta_zero1@}\).

Your second zero: \(\displaystyle {@ta_zero2@}\).

Your third zero: \(\displaystyle {@ta_zero3@}\).

Step 3: Vertical asymptotes

Vertical asymptotes occur when the argument of the tangent function equals \(\displaystyle \frac{\pi}{2}+n\pi\).

Thus,

\(2x=\frac{\pi}{2}+n\pi\).

Dividing by \(2\) gives

\(\displaystyle x=\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{n\pi}{2}\).

The two vertical asymptotes nearest the origin are \(\displaystyle x=-\frac{\pi}{4}\) and \(\displaystyle x=\frac{\pi}{4}\).

Your left asymptote: \(\displaystyle {@ta_asymL@}\).

Your right asymptote: \(\displaystyle {@ta_asymR@}\).
